- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope afterward.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates future values; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or use sentiment-weighted smoothing.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.2–0.8) and price is volatile, model exhibits mean-reversion bias; apply a 3–5 day lag correction: forecast = prior 3-day average + sentiment-adjusted drift.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward trends in low-sentiment periods; add 2–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment <0.3 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a peak, model fails to anticipate reversal; add a 1–2 day “sentiment decay” penalty to forecast slope.
